executive_summary: The dominant thread running through today's content is the theme of high-stakes competition producing unexpected or turbulent outcomes across vastly different arenas. At Roland Garros, another upset has shaken the tennis world, while in basketball, the San Antonio Spurs' elimination of the Oklahoma City Thunder — widely considered a powerhouse — to reach the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks signals that this championship cycle is being defined by surprises rather than predetermined favorites. The Economist's coverage of China's solar industry adds a parallel dimension: even the world's most dominant industrial competitor is experiencing internal disruption, suggesting that commanding positions — whether on a sports court or a global market — are far less stable than they appear. Across sports and economics alike, today's content makes a unified argument that entrenched advantages are being rapidly destabilized, and that the institutions or players who seemed most secure are the ones most exposed to sudden reversals.

items.headline: Defending champ goes down
items.blurb: Coco Gauff's French Open title defense ended Saturday, on the court where she collapsed to the clay a year ago as the winner of a second Grand Slam title. Anastasia Potapova, the 25-year-old Russian-turned-Austrian who has blasted her way back to relevance this spring, came back from a set down to outlast Gauff (4) on arguably her best surface 4-6, 7-6(1), 6-4 during a strange evening on the tournament's main stage.

items.headline: That's enough sets!
items.blurb: The player most associated with this French Open years from now may well be João Fonseca. Because the 19-year-old Brazilian was already such a promising young figure in men's tennis, and because Novak Djokovic is an all-time great, Fonseca's five-set win Friday could take on heavy meaning in the years to come, à la Roger Federer's upset of Pete Sampras at Wimbledon in 2001. If that's the case, what to make of Juan Manuel Cerúndolo? The world No. 56 from Argentina arguably deserves a spot in the history books for backing up his upset of world No. 1 Jannik Sinner on Thursday with a marathon win of his own Saturday.

newsletters.title: China’s world-beating solar industry is in turmoil

items.headline: China's world-beating solar industry is in turmoil
items.blurb: China's solar industry is notorious for its busts. But the current slump is of a different order. Although an energy crunch caused by the war in Iran has boosted the country's solar exports, that will be small cheer to its companies, which face dimming domestic demand, a glut of solar-panel supply and rising protectionism in Western markets. Most have run at a loss for years. After blistering growth, the world's solar factory faces a reckoning.

items.headline: The world's top condom-maker is getting squeezed
items.blurb: A very different type of company is struggling to perform: Karex, the world's top condom-maker. The company's share price is down by a third since the start of the year. Tariffs, budget cuts and the weakening dollar have sapped the firm of its virility.
